issues.description: Function 'set_pixel': the problem statement requires that the pixel coordinates are passed as x in EAX and y in EBX and that no registers other than EAX are changed by set_pixel. The solution implementation of set_pixel (solution_repository/pixel.asm) performs 'xchg eax, ebx' (swapping x and y) and uses/pushes/pops EBX, ESI and EDX inside the routine. This contradicts the specification: the solution effectively expects the parameters in swapped registers and does not preserve registers other than EAX, which will confuse students about the correct calling convention and the register-preservation requirement and can lead to incorrect behavior when the template and spec are followed.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's set_pixel conform to the specification: accept x in EAX and y in EBX and ensure that no registers other than EAX are changed on return. Concretely, remove the 'xchg eax, ebx' and any code that leaves EBX/ECX/EDI/etc. modified; if temporary registers are needed (EDX, ESI, etc.), push them at the start of set_pixel and pop them before returning so their caller-visible values are preserved. An example approach: push edx / push esi, compute x*4 and y*7680 using EAX and temporary registers, add display_start to form the address in EAX (or move the final address into a preserved temporary and write [addr] <- ECX), then pop esi / pop edx and ret. Alternatively, if the solution intentionally expects swapped parameters or different preservation rules, update the problem statement and template comment to state that explicitly.
